## Observed defect
On origin/main 2ca3e28fcc6, `pytest tests/unit/test_reclaim_resign.py -k test_resign_makes_enforced_verify_pass_with_era_keys` fails (reproduced locally on macOS and in Gerrit CI on ubuntu py3.11, py3.12 and py3.13, runs 44728882402 and 44728890345):

```
tests/unit/test_reclaim_resign.py:382
assert {f["verdict"] for f in failing} == {"unsigned", "bad-signature"}
AssertionError: assert {'signer-not-...', 'unsigned'} == {'bad-signature', 'unsigned'}
```

## Cause (from history)
- `9a6ed375112` "Classify off-keyring signers apart from forgeries" (starving-sphalerite-skua) changed `verify-identity` so a sound signature by a key that is not on the claimed author's keyring reports `signer-not-on-keyring` instead of `bad-signature`.
- `717c50f8b33` "Re-sign failing events during the reclaim collapse" (minimum-seedy-lowchen) added this test expecting the old `bad-signature` verdict for the fixture's off-keyring events. The two landed independently, so main is red on this test.

## Impact
Every Gerrit change whose CI runs the default pytest tier gets `Verified -1` until this is fixed (seen on 3472 and 3473).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_reclaim_resign.py -q` passes on main, with the failing-verdict expectation matching the current verify-identity vocabulary (`signer-not-on-keyring` for a sound off-keyring signature) or the fixture producing a genuine forgery if `bad-signature` is what the test means to exercise.
- [x] `make verify` is green and the fix lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
